ModuleName: 14 - Content Management Systems, Webmaster Roles, and Site Maintenance

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the module's learning topics spanning CMS fundamentals (definition, core components, ecosystem role), comparisons of major platforms (WordPress, Joomla, Drupal), and decision-making between CMS and custom builds, serving as a navigational overview for learners and instructors to understand the scope and sequence of the module.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: A navigation page listing all topics covered in the module — Introduction to CMS, popular platforms, CMS vs. custom builds, the webmaster role, and site maintenance — giving learners and instructors an at-a-glance outline of the module's structure.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to Content Management Systems
Artifacts.Description: A foundational reading that explains what a Content Management System is, how it stores and presents content, and why CMS platforms are the standard solution for building and managing modern websites; learners read it before exploring specific platforms.

Artifacts.Name: Popular CMS Platforms and Their Features
Artifacts.Description: A comparative overview of major CMS platforms (such as WordPress, Drupal, and others), examining their core features, strengths, and typical use cases to help learners and instructors evaluate which platform suits different project types.

Artifacts.Name: CMS vs. Custom Builds: Choosing the Right Approach
Artifacts.Description: A decision-focused reading that weighs the trade-offs between using an existing CMS and building a fully custom web application, covering strategic, technical, and business factors; learners use it to develop a framework for making platform decisions on real projects.

Artifacts.Name: The Webmaster Role and Professional Responsibilities
Artifacts.Description: A reading that defines the webmaster role, its scope of responsibilities — spanning technical maintenance, content oversight, and organizational communication — and how it differs from pure development or content-editing roles; learners use it to understand the profession's breadth.

Artifacts.Name: Website Maintenance and Production Management
Artifacts.Description: A reading covering the ongoing practices required to keep a live website secure, performant, accurate, and reliable, including maintenance routines, production management workflows, and strategies for handling updates and incidents; learners use it as a practical guide to post-launch site care.
